thread:
maya: Quick sync on the webinar / benchmark narrative. Need two strong chart hooks + 3 short messaging variants for social and the signup page. Can we lock visuals by EOD so design can start?

jon: Locking numbers depends on infravalidation. Use placeholders like <P95_MS> and <COST_PER_1K>. I can provide provisional CSV by 11:30.

sergio: I sketched 3 chart types:
- Chart A: Latency curve (p50/p95) vs token throughput line overlay. Good for ops teams.
- Chart B: Cost per 1k tokens (bars) across model/quantization variants; add an annotation showing "same quality" zone.
- Chart C: Routing waterfall: percent served by cheap variant vs fallback, with latency distribution stacked. Good for product/exec.

maya: Love Chart C as a hero for the site. It tells the routing story without heavy numbers. We'll still show Chart B in the deck for procurement economics.

elaine: Messaging: need 3 hero lines for the landing A/B. Short, benefit-first. My drafts:
  1) "Same responses. Lower inference spend."
  2) "Reduce per-token cost without rewrites."
  3) "Keep latency predictable, cut unit economics."

katie: For social snippets, shorter is better. Examples: 
  - "Cut inference cost. Keep latency steady."
  - "2x cheaper per token at the same p95 (example)."

jon: Don't say "2x" until we vet with infra. Use "up to 2x" or leave numeric placeholder. Also define what we mean by "per-token": do we include prefix caching? Outline in footnote.

sergio: Design notes: palette should be Redwood green for positive bars, muted gray for baseline. Use small callouts for the slices we recommend (short chat, long instruction, embeddings). Add microcopy: "Measured on public LLMs + Redwood routing".

maya: For the webinar slide deck we need: 1) one-slide problem statement, 2) one-slide benchmark results (Chart B + Chart A inset), 3) cost breakdown example (CSV sample), 4) customer Q&A script.

elaine: I'll draft the customer Q&A script. Key expected questions: "Does this change model outputs?" "How do you handle cache invalidation?" "What's the SLA?"

maya: Draft answers:
  Q: "Does this change outputs?"
  A: "No application changes. Routing favors compatible variants and preserves model logits ordering; we validate with evals and flag regressions."

  Q: "Cache invalidation?"
  A: "We provide TTL controls and traceable invalidation events; customers can tune per-route policies."

  Q: "SLA?"
  A: "Hosted customers get documented latency SLOs; Dedicated/Private options have contractual SLAs."

jon: CSV fields for bench upload: model, variant, quant, workload, p50_ms, p95_ms, throughput_tps, cost_per_1k_tokens, tokens_per_request, notes. I'll export as sample.

katie: Landing CTA options: "Get a quick cost chart" vs "See a benchmark for your app." Which converts better? Suggest we A/B test.

maya: Agree. A/B test CTAs and hero lines. Also want small form ask: "avg request size (tokens)" to auto-tailor the cost chart.

sergio: For visuals I recommend annotating p95 hotspots and adding a tiny legend explaining "routing share". Also include a tiny footnote: "Benchmark run on <HARDWARE> with batching and caching enabled."

maya: One more ask: legal wants a short qualifier for the site: "Results vary by workload; contact us for a tailored analysis." Add to footer.

jon: I'll confirm numbers and hardware details. Expect an "approved" comment here by noon.

maya: Timeline: drafts for deck + site copy by tomorrow morning. Design to follow once charts locked. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
